title: SEDATE: Do Large Language Models Share an Aggression Circuit Across Languages?
abstract: arXiv:2610.33542v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As the applications of AI continue to expand across various multimodal and multilingual domains, ensuring safe and responsible deployment of these systems has become an important concern. A wide-range of interventions have been proposed to make AI responses safer and more reliable. They often incur substantial computational or annotation costs, or cannot be extended to multilingual settings. In this work, we propose Selective Detection And Targeted Editing (SEDATE), a training-free approach based on detect-edit-verify strategy. SEDATE first detects the responsible neurons, edits them as and when necessary and finally verifies the model responses; all without any additional model training. We evaluate SEDATE across 7 languages and 4 model families. We further evaluate its effectiveness across 4 out-of-distribution languages and 4 additional datasets. We show that SEDATE achieves substantially superior safety scores across all languages

translated_title: SEDATE：大型语言模型是否在跨语言间共享攻击性回路？
translated_abstract: 随着人工智能的应用在各种多模态和多语言领域不断扩展，确保这些系统安全且负责任地部署已成为一个重要问题。为使AI响应更加安全可靠，研究者们已提出多种干预方法，但这些方法通常需要高昂的计算或标注成本，或无法扩展到多语言场景。在本工作中，我们提出了选择性检测与定向编辑（SEDATE），这是一种基于“检测-编辑-验证”策略的免训练方法。SEDATE首先检测出负责相关行为的神经元，在必要时对其进行编辑，最后验证模型响应，全程无需任何额外的模型训练。我们在7种语言和4个模型家族上对SEDATE进行了评估，并进一步在4种分布外语言和4个额外数据集上验证了其有效性。结果表明，SEDATE在所有语言上都取得了显著更优的安全分数。
tldr: SEDATE提出了一种免训练的“检测-编辑-验证”方法，通过定位并编辑与攻击性相关的神经元，使大型语言模型在7种语言及分布外场景中均显著提升了安全性。
en_tdlr: SEDATE is a training-free detect-edit-verify approach that locates and edits neurons responsible for aggression, substantially improving LLM safety across 7 languages and out-of-distribution settings.
